ov: The only domesticated member of the cat family. Cats were first tamed from the African wildcat in the Near East around 7500 BCE, and there are now an estimated 600 million worldwide.

why.ac: Cats are crepuscular, most active around dawn and dusk, though pet cats partly adjust to their owners’ hours.
why.p: The only domesticated member of the cat family.

len: About 46 cm, plus a tail of about 30 cm
rg: Worldwide alongside people, and as feral cats living wild, which have driven declines in native birds, mammals and reptiles.
df: An obligate carnivore that needs a mainly meat diet. A solitary hunter of small prey such as mice and rats.

cf.tip: A European wildcat is bigger and more heavily built, with a bushy, blunt tail ringed with two or three black bands and a black tip.

fx: It can hear sounds too faint or too high-pitched for human ears, such as those made by small mammals.
